title: Publishers Response To AI Highlights Why Gaming Industry Is Behind
author: bingewavecinema
selftext:
While the gaming space, particularly indie games, constantly tests new ideas, AAA studios tend to release safer bets. But when it comes to AI and business innovation, the industry often acts like it wants to stay in the 1800s.

I sent a publisher this video: [https://youtu.be/B2ASCTomtIA](https://youtu.be/B2ASCTomtIA)

I understand why people are get angry about AI stealing artwork or causing talented people to lose their jobs. Those are legit concerns.

But using AI for development and business operations is different.

A lot of code is already open source and publicly available. Before AI, people copied and pasted answers from Stack Overflow that someone else had already figured out. Now, AI helps speed up that same process without digging through 15 wrong answers.

For business, AI is about drastically increasing the speed at which someone can research, analyze, and create useful output.

I think in five years, we are going to see a new kind of game developer and publisher emerge: one that can simply outmaneuver the people who are stuck being anti-AI about everything.

Someone once told me, “Not using AI is like riding a bicycle in a motorcycle race.”

comments.author: psdwizzard
comments.body: I build ai tools for AAA game company for living. Big developers are using ai, we just are not loud about it.

comments.author: DumbestEngineer4U
comments.body: In gamedev, the development itself wasn’t a major bottleneck, especially for indies. You can make a quality game with very little development budget. The problem was marketing, IP, or making  something that actually sells. None of which AI is going to help you with. If anything it will overcrowd most platforms with slop making it harder to get noticed.

replies.author: bingewavecinema
replies.body:
That is where the fundamental gap is understanding what A+ + Marketing really does, which isn't about slop or making anything. Its about faster understanding.

One of the biggest task in marketing is processing LOTS of data to make data-driven about where and how to execute.

For example, lets see you want a to find a journalist to write about your game. You have too:  
\- Research relevant publications and why they are fit  
\- Then research the writes who work their and their past work to figure who is best to pitch  
\- Formulate a pitch

That can take 30 minutes or over an hour for a single pitch to go out to gather, anaylize and draft something relevant.

OR, AI can gather all the information for you and present it in a way that allows you to make a decision in 5 minutes. Its not slop, its faster decision making if you value your time.

comments.author: ponderdiggums
comments.body:
1) The gaming industry is a creative space, not enterprise software. Your language suggests a different approach. You claim the entire gaming industry is 'behind', and pine for a future when studios that embrace AI 'outmaneuver' the 'people who are stuck being anti ai'. This is a red flag to many of us, not only does it suggest a strange culture war position but it comes off as arrogant and disrespectful. I probably would have declined to work with you on that merit alone. 

2) Even if an Indie studio isn't anti-AI, they're definitely not spending their likely strict budget on tools they could make themselves for free. I can't speak to other developers, but I'm never paying for any tools again. I can make what I need with Claude Code on a whim.

replies.author: bingewavecinema
replies.body:
Then you are failing into the trap, because you are still are paying in tokens and time. And there is where operating like a business can distinguish.

For example, lets say you want to have something that helps with scheduling meetings. You can get calendly for $10 to $20 a month.

Or you can build your own calendar tool. It will probably take about a week or two to get al the edge cases covered, testing done and many of the nuicances that are required. You'll also probably spend $500 to $1k in token for usage plans OR its you can still for $20 plans but then you are competing on your limited token usage that you want to spend into your gamedev.

If something cost $10 a month, that is $120 a year and no time. It will take you 4 years of using it to where your AI product you made becomes worth it.

comments.author: poponis

comments.author: perrinashcroft
comments.body:
AI is being used in AAA in all sorts of ways, though obviously most are trying to steer clear of the generative art that players hate the most. 

Your tool would be dead on arrival at any major studio because if there's any value here it would be much more sensible to get one internal dev to make it themselves so they can customise and adjust it to fit their own specific needs and give them reassurance of their privacy. Studios have plenty of tools devs for exactly this kind of reason. 

Sure you've already done the work and spent the tokens, but that kind of budget is peanuts even at indie levels. Yes paying you $10 a month might be cheaper but when marketing their game studios are looking for the best option, not the cheapest.

This is one of the core problems with trying to sell SaaS in the vibe coding era. You've got to find customers who have enough to pay you a subscription but don't have enough money to just get an internal dev to replicate it. That's going to be a tough window to find.

replies.author: bingewavecinema
replies.body:
Actually the product isn't designed for AAA who builds everything internally, I'm well aware they build everything internally.

This is designed for indies who struggle with needing to generate awareness for their games but have to make harder choices:

\- I market games and work with other agencies; cost for market or agencies can be from $1k to $15k a month. Indies don't have the budget, so do they do no marketing or build a tool for themselves?

\- Build it yourself; do indies really know what they are building? How the process actually works with ads? Influencers? PR? Other forms of marketing? Developing the wrong solution can happen, developing and maintaning the right solution takes both time and tokens, is that really worth or it?

I built this product pre-vibe coding error, so I know the complexities in and out. Now when I started to do vibe coding, I've probably put upwards of $10k of tokens into just optimizing it for marketing.

This is where the customer has to figure out, do I pay $10 or do I pay in token +time that can exceed a few thousand?

Not just in gaming but the vibe coding trap in general; knowing when you should build it yourself or pay for something else.

replies.author: perrinashcroft
replies.body:
Well I was responding to your opening comment:

"While the gaming space, particularly indie games, constantly tests new ideas, AAA studios tend to release safer bets. But when it comes to AI and business innovation, the industry often acts like it wants to stay in the 1800s."

I'm explaining why I don't think that's true. They are adopting AI in all sorts of business functions.

Even with the indie space I still think it's a hard market fit because mid to large budget indie projects are already backed by publishers wont need your tools since publishers have established relationships with press and influencers. Those kind of connections are obviously better than using AI to build your email spam list.

So your main market has to be small indies who have the skills to build games but not the skills the vibe code something like this.

Best of luck but I think it's going to be a tough sell.

replies.author: bingewavecinema
replies.body:
I should clarify what I meant, AAA game take safer bets in the games the release. Proven titles and franchise. Indies are far more creative in taking risk where new ideas in games are constantly emerging.

When it comes to publishers, less than 1% of games getting funding, and the number is growing smaller as returns become more questionable.

So the goal here is to give the 99% of the market that won't get a publisher the ability to better compete while not losing focus on development.
